newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria oil funding crisis meet put off - ministry.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria oil funding crisis meet put off - ministry.

text.p: A crucial meeting between Nigeria's oil joint venture partners and senior government officials to discuss a funding crisis has been adjourned until next week, the oil ministry said on Wednesday.

"All I can say is that it has been adjourned," oil ministry spokesman Gbenga Onayiga told journalists in the capital Abuja. He did not say on what day next week the meeting would take place or explain why the meeting was adjourned.

Chief executives of the joint venture partners went into the oil ministry for the talks. But it was unclear whether they had been able to meet either minister Dan Etete or the other senior government officials with whom talks were planned.

Oil industry officials say current production, of more than two million barrels per day, could be cut by as much as five percent in 1997 if an increase to their funding is not approved. They say long term effects would be even more serious.
The joint venture partners complain they have been forced to cut back new projects, maintenance and exploration after an across the board cut to $2.05 billion from a proposed $3.32 billion budget.
State-run Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation owns an average 57 percent stake in joint-ventures with Royal Dutch/Shell, Mobil Corp., Chevron, Elf Aquitaine, Texaco and Agip.
